To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
slow oscillations are generated by the interaction between network-mediated and metabolic-mediated mechanisms.
the membrane potential of cortical neurons, in part governed by ATP-modulating potassium (KATP) channels, is an interface between neuronal metabolism and network responsivity.

slow oscillations between periods of high cortical activity and low cortical activity in mammals result from interactions between neuronal network activity and neuronal metabolism, mediated by ATP-modulated K(ATP) potassium channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the regulation of cortical response state, and how these mechanisms are affected by anesthesia.
the question of how the level of arousal is regulated in mammalian cortex and how this process is influenced by the neuronal network.
the mechanisms that underlie the transition between sleep and wake states in mammals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neuronal network activity and metabolic state interact to generate the slow oscillation of network responsivity.
the K(ATP) channel is a key player in the regulation of the response state of the brain.
the neuronal network is the main player in the control of the cortical network response state, and the metabolic state is the main player to control neuronal excitability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neuronal metabolic state governs the cortical network response state via the K(ATP) channel.

the level of arousal in the mammalian cortex is a consequence of a balance between excitatory network-mediated mechanisms, involving slow kainate receptor-dependent events, and neuronal metabolism-related homeostatic mechanisms, involving ATP-dependent potassium channels.
neuronal network activity and metabolic state interact to determine the cortical network response state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level of arousal in the cortex is not a simple reflection of metabolic state.
the neuronal metabolic state and the cortical response state are coupled via ATP-dependent homeostasis, with the K(ATP) channel serving as an interface.
cortical responsivity is not a static property of the network, but a dynamic property of the network and its interactions with the metabolic state of the cell.
